claims.claim: Paper formalises only the pine cone; wheat awns, flytrap, nacre, seed pods carry no equation; eq 6 gives no numerical tau, chi, m0.
claims.source_says: Here we instantiate Nat on the hygromorphic pinecone hierarchy as an example of a natural system
claims.note: Fetched page (first 100k of 126k chars) confirms pinecone-only equations and symbolic eq 6; the rest of the text was not read, so absence elsewhere is unconfirmed.

claims.claim: 'Preserve dynamics' is the simulation condition; only composition closure is proved, fidelity left to experiment; repo 'verified' flag is a tolerance test, only equilibrium angles measured.
claims.source_says: Here, verification is a claim about composition, not about any single model.
claims.note: Paper side supported (commutes with time evolution, chain-rule closure, fidelity empirical); I did not read spec.py's flag or measurement claims.

claims.claim: Lean re-run: HygromorphCeilingCheck and Hygromorphs compile with errors=0, no sorryAx; ceiling f<=3/(2h), bilayer_rules_out; list of checked/unchecked items.
claims.source_says: theorem bilayer_rules_out (h m n Δε κ_claimed : ℝ) ... (hclaim : 3 / 2 * Δε / h < κ_claimed) : bilayerCurvature h m n Δε < κ_claimed
claims.note: Theorem statement matches the ceiling claim and no sorry appears in the check file; the cited logs path does not exist, and I did not verify the rest of the list or the 'not in paper' point.

claims.claim: Prop A.25 needs tau_L=tau_T=tau_Delta and equal moisture, unstated in paper; with tau_L=1, tau_T=5 two states give dD/dt -0.0095 and -0.0895; conjugacy fixes tau so F cannot cover time-constant change.
claims.source_says: It does not state positivity, magnitudes, or any other conditions on them. The proof does not depend on their values.
claims.note: Re-running closure_check.py reproduced -0.0095 and -0.0895 and the equal-tau case; the paper's silence on tau conditions is confirmed, but the necessity argument and the F/conjugacy point are the agent's own and not checked.

overall: The paper-based claims largely hold, and the arithmetic reproduces. The Lean theorem statement matches, but the logs the agent cites are missing and two claims rest partly on the agent's own reasoning.
